robot: Zero-shiki Jinki ver.2.0 / Multifunctional Railway Heavy Machine
robot_native: 零式人機 ver.2.0 / 多機能鉄道重機
company: Jinki Ittai (developer/licensor) + Nippon Signal (manufacturer) + JR West (customer)
company_native: 株式会社人機一体・日本信号・JR西日本
target_applications: railway overhead-line maintenance: structure painting, obstructing-tree cutting at height; roadmap: power transmission, civil engineering

base_type.value: humanoid torso on telescoping crane boom of road-rail vehicle (no self-locomotion)

height_mm.source: n/a (torso dimensions not disclosed); working height up to 12,000mm above ground

battery_kwh.source: powered from road-rail vehicle (no battery constraint)

actuators.value: high-power actuation with force/torque control and power-amplified bilateral control (type n/a)

end_effector.value: interchangeable heavy tools: powered cutters/saws, painting equipment; 40kg grip

media_at_flange.value: tool power supplied via boom/vehicle (details n/a)

sensors_head.value: head cameras streamed to operator VR goggles (robot's-eye view)

sensors_wrist_hand.value: force/torque sensing feeding bilateral force-feedback loop

software_stack.value: power-amplified bilateral master-slave teleoperation (Jinki Ittai patented stack); no autonomy/AI layer

safety_compliance.value: removes workers from fall/electrocution risk at height; operator in safe cabin; rail operational approval implied by revenue service; formal certs n/a

price.source: n/a (not disclosed; Jinki Ittai monetizes via patent licensing to Nippon Signal)

availability.value: Japan, JR West network; via Nippon Signal as integrated maintenance vehicle

deployment_evidence.value: revenue service on JR West operating lines since 07/2024 (painting, tree cutting); operated by Nishi-Nippon Electric Systems; ver.1.3 displayed at Fukushima Robot Test Field; unit count n/a (est. single-digit)

notes: Category coinage 人型重機 'humanoid heavy machinery'. Business model: IP licensing (force/torque + power-amplified bilateral control patents), manufacturing by partners. Mecha styling by Shoji Kawamori (Macross).
